translations.text: Many are the gifts on earth, new and plain to see, which living souls carry in their minds. In the same way, here the God of hosts, the Creator strong in power, deals them out to men. He gives special gifts and sends his own abundance far and wide, and every one of those who dwell among the people may receive a share of it.
There is no man on earth so unfortunate, nor so lacking in means, so small-minded, nor so slow of mind, that the Giver of gifts deprives him entirely of skills of mind or of mighty deeds,

of wisdom in understanding or in speech, so that he may not despair of all the things that He made in this worldly life, of every one of the gifts. God never decrees that anyone should become so wretched.

Nor, on the other hand, does anyone rise so high through the power of wisdom among the people, in the glory of this life, that the Guardian of peoples, through his holy grace, sends him here wise thoughts and worldly skills
and lets them all come under the power of one man, so that he, full of glorious gifts, a man strong in mind, may not turn beyond measure out of pride and then despise those of poorer means;
but He who has the power of judgement distributes variously throughout this middle-earth skills of body to the people, to the dwellers in the land.
To one here on earth He grants possessions, worldly treasures. Another is poor in means, a man of hard fortune, yet he is wise in skills of mind.
One receives greater bodily strength. One is noble and fair in form. One is a poet, gifted in songs. One is ready of speech.
One is a hunter who drives the proud [?] wild beasts. One is dear to a man rich in worldly goods. One is hardy in war, a warrior skilled in battle, where shields clash.
One can devise the people's counsel in an assembly among the wise-minded, where many wise men are gathered together.

One can skilfully plan the building of every kind of lofty structure; his hand is trained, skilled and controlled, as is right for a craftsman, to set up a hall; he knows how to join a wide building firmly against sudden collapse.
One can touch the harp with his hands; he has the skill of quick movements on the glee-wood.
One is a runner, one a sure shot, one skilled in songs, one swift on land, fast of foot.
One steers the prow on the dusky wave and knows the way of the current, leader of the crew over the wide sea, when the sea-bold men pull the oars with swift strength near the ship's side.
One is a swimmer; one is skilled in working gold and gems, when the lord of men commands him to adorn a treasure for his glory.

One, a smith skilled of mind, can make many weapons of war, useful in battle, when he forges for the fighting of men a helmet or a hip-knife or a war-mailcoat, a bright sword or the boss of a shield, firmly joined against the flight of the spear.
One is kind and eager to give alms, virtuous in his ways. One is a quick and ready servant in the mead-hall.
One knows about horses and is wise in horsemanship. One, controlled of mind, endures with patience what he must.
One knows judgments, where the lord's men consider counsel. One is quick at the board game.
One is witty at the wine-drinking, a good keeper of the beer. One is good at building, at raising a dwelling. One is a commander, a bold leader of the army. One is a counsellor of the people.
One is a thane among bold-minded men, standing by his lord in time of need. One has patience, a steadfast spirit. One is a fowler, skilled with the hawk. One is bold on horseback.
One is very swift and has an artful kind of sport, the gift of entertaining before the retainers, light and supple of limb. One is friendly and has a mind and words agreeable to men.
One here eagerly takes to heart the needs of the soul, and chooses for himself the Lord's favour above all earthly wealth.
One is brave in the struggle against the devil, and is always ready to fight against sins.

One has skill in many church services. He can praise the Ruler of life aloud in hymns, and has a lofty, clear voice. One is learned in books and steadfast in learning. One is skilful with his hands at writing down the mysteries of words.
There is now no man on earth so skilled in mind, nor so great in strength, that all these gifts should ever be given to him alone,
So that pride may not harm him, nor his mind swell up because of that glory, if he alone above all men has beauty and wisdom and success in his works;

instead, God restrains the human race from pride in various ways and distributes his gifts. To some he gives them in virtues, to some in skills, to some in beauty, to some in war. To some men he gives a gentle heart and a virtuous mind. One is loyal to his lord.
So the Lord sows his benefits widely and worthily. May he always have glory and radiant praise for this, he who gives us this life and shows his gentle mind to men.
